target_customer: Fintechs and technology companies that need direct bank connectivity through an API
problem: Building financial products on top of legacy banks is slow and opaque. Increase offers an API to move money over ACH, wires, cards, checks and real-time rails directly connected to the Federal Reserve.
business_model: Usage based API fees on payments, with later bank ownership

founders.name: Darragh Buckley
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch calls him a strong engineer and Stripe's first employee. YC page lists him as the only founder.

competitors.name: Treasury Prime
competitors.what: Banking APIs connecting fintechs to multiple partner banks
competitors.traction_then: Working with partner banks; announced Series A May 2020
competitors.funding_then: $9M Series A in May 2020 on top of a $2.5M seed, $11.5M total

technical_complexity.rationale: Direct connections to payment rails, bank sponsors and the Federal Reserve needed deep payments and compliance engineering for a very small team.

defensibility.rationale: Bank relationships, rail certifications and deep customer integrations are hard to copy, and later bank ownership strengthened this.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Stripe became a customer and Increase partner rather than a rival. Synapse went bankrupt in 2024, which helped direct providers.

market_need_then: Fintech API providers were drawing capital in 2020; TechCrunch tied Treasury Prime's round to the wave of API deals after Visa's Plaid deal. Increase's customers later included Ramp, Gusto and Stripe.

branding.name_origin: Started under the placeholder name bnk.dev, an intentionally bad name until a good domain was available, per an Increase engineer quoted by Domain Name Wire (2022).
branding.domain_note: Acquired increase.com in early 2021 per Whois records; it had a $150,000 asking price on Sedo and the price paid was not disclosed.

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer first, plain technical language about moving money with code.

branding.brand_signature: Exact match increase.com domain acquired after starting as bnk.dev

rebrands.why: Working name was intentionally weak until the increase.com domain could be bought, per Domain Name Wire.

branding.community_and_virality: Domain Name Wire covered the domain story; engineers cited Paul Graham's essay on changing your name.

brand_strength.rationale: Trusted by well known fintechs and covered by TechCrunch and Banking Dive, with a deliberate exact match domain, but the brand is developer focused and not consumer known.

outcome_analysis: Increase appears to have grown without public venture rounds, with a founder who spent six years at Stripe and customers such as Ramp, Gusto and Stripe. In July 2026 it launched its own bank after acquiring Twin City Bancorp, approved by the San Francisco Fed in June 2025. Its direct rail connections and the 2024 Synapse failure helped it, though funding history is not public.
notes: CB Insights lists a convertible note and $500K total with Y Combinator; Techlist estimates $7M. Both are aggregator figures and conflict with a profile claim of self-funded, so no round is recorded. TechCrunch (2025) and Banking Dive (2026) mention no funding rounds. The Business Wire launch release returned 403. Increase engineer Jack Flintermann appears in Domain Name Wire but is not called a co-founder. Column (bought a bank in 2021) is a competitor but its source is later than the batch. The company's 'self-funded and profitable in 2025' claim is from a single search summary.
